review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read the definitions it depends on in FiniteTargetHomColimit.lean: stageHom, stageHomClass, stageHomFunctor, stageHomPost, stageHomNatIso, and the stageHomEquiv API. The target's new definitions are stageHomLimitMap and stageHomLimitEquiv, which are the bijection between continuous maps c.pt ⟶ d.pt and sections of G ⋙ stageHomFunctor F. They are built from Mathlib's Cone, IsLimit.homEquiv, compCoyonedaSectionsEquiv and Functor.sections, so they reuse Mathlib's API and do not compete with it. I searched Mathlib's CategoryTheory directory for pro-object or limit-of-coyoneda concepts. I found Types/Yoneda, IndYoneda and Galois/Prorepresentability. None provides an equivalent for profinite spaces and finite-space diagrams. The named equivalence is a useful specialisation, and I found no concrete cost from duplication.
